consideredAndRejected.reason: Owner-registration-GATED is not owner-CAUSED. The realistic trigger is an upgradeable registered token changing implementation after registration - outside the owner's control. Footgun test: would a competent, non-malicious owner be SURPRISED that registering a token lets that token make every annihilation of the pair exceed the block gas limit? YES. Surprise => footgun => in scope. PROVEN by measurement (16,782 gas for a 32-byte answer vs 158,677,386 for 6.4MB).

Three enumerated triggers, and T3 (an honest token whose decimals() is not view-callable) is not owner error at all - it is PROVEN by Tier2Delta.t.sol::test_statefulDecimalsBricksHonestToken. The owner would reasonably assume the minter's own registered decimals field is the authority; the link to 'the reward leg is unrealisable for every holder of this pair' is not obvious from either contract, and the fault is INVISIBLE on the minter's own mint path. Surprise => footgun => in scope as an operational hazard with safe-config guidance.

Registering a hook-bearing token is owner-gated, but the consequence (one wei of phUSD donated inside the window permanently bricks annihilation for that pair) is non-obvious, and the nonReentrant guard plus the ReentrantStable mock may reasonably read as having settled the hook-token question - they settle RE-ENTRY, not third-party DONATION. Footgun, in scope.

Its whole operational value is to stop ledger F-01 being closed on false evidence. Under the standing principle that falsely-exhaustive in-source docs RAISE severity, it is kept - and kept SEPARATE from F-01, because folding it in would make the tripwire invisible inside the finding it protects.

carveOutApplied.whyTheClassLabelAloneWasNOTSUFFICIENT: USDT IS an explicit carve-out on this engagement and USDT carries an owner-enablable fee mechanism (currently zero). Disposing of the whole fee-on-transfer class in one move would therefore have suppressed the one token the carve-out protects. The deduplicator was right to refuse the blanket move, and it is refused here too.
carveOutApplied.affirmativeDisproofForUSDTSPECIFICALLY: The fail-closed chain was traced in source at c91bc1a (src/Antimatter.sol:246-254) with a NON-ZERO USDT fee assumed live, and it holds on TWO independent legs. Leg 1 (incoming): safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, this, stableAmount) credits stableAmount - fee. Antimatter then forceApproves and the minter pulls the FULL stableAmount at :251; with no pre-existing balance the pull reverts for insufficient balance. Leg 2 (residue): if a prior donation covers the shortfall so the pull succeeds, the contract's post-state balance is stableBefore - fee, which is != stableBefore, so `if (IERC20(stable).balanceOf(address(this)) != stableBefore) revert StableNotDeposited()` at :254 fires. In BOTH legs the transaction reverts in full and the burn at :239 is reverted with it. There is no state in which the antimatter is burned and the stable leg is under-delivered, so SA-003's premise - that subsequent logic ASSUMES a delivery it did not get - is factually false at this commit.
carveOutApplied.verdict: The C4 known-invalid carve-out for fee-on-transfer tokens is applied, but ONLY after the USDT-specific fail-closed chain was confirmed by reading the code. The disposal rests on the disproof; the class label is the secondary ground, not the primary one.

residualNotSuppressed.residual: AVAILABILITY, not accounting. If Tether ever enables a non-zero fee on a REGISTERED USDT, every annihilation of that pair reverts (StableNotDeposited or an insufficient-balance revert inside minter.mint) until the owner registers an alternative stablecoin. Nothing is lost or stolen, and the revert precedes nothing irreversible - but the reward leg for that pair becomes unrealisable, and the fault is invisible on the minter's own mint path.

findings.title: Verified false-positive / inert / Law-3-inventory static results on src/Antimatter.sol - disposed on the record, not by silence
findings.sanitizerReview: All nine items re-read. Eight carry an affirmative disproof, an in-code mooting, or an explicit Law-3 inventory basis and are UPHELD as disposed. Only SA-012 rested on a C4 known-invalid CLASS rather than a disproof, and the deduplicator correctly routed it here rather than asserting the disposal itself. Adjudicated below.

sa012Adjudication.verdict: INVALID - disposed on TWO grounds, the in-code mooting being the primary one.
sa012Adjudication.primaryGroundInCodeMooting: A zero-value transfer is UNREACHABLE on the annihilate path at c91bc1a, verified in source. (a) :222 `if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount()`. (b) toStableAmount cannot return zero: stableAmount = amount / scale, and `if (stableAmount * scale != amount) revert AmountNotRepresentable(...)` at :299 means a stableAmount of 0 requires amount == 0, already excluded - so the :246 safeTransferFrom is always non-zero. (c) :261's safeTransfer moves mintedForStable, which equals expectedForStable, which is non-zero because `if (expectedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived()` at :235 fires pre-burn. (d) :308 is rescueERC20 with an owner-supplied amount - an owner passing zero is an obvious, harmless no-op and is Law-3 trusted.
sa012Adjudication.secondaryGroundC4Class: Tokens that revert on zero-value transfers are weird-ERC20 behaviour, a C4 known-invalid class.
sa012Adjudication.usdtCarveOutChecked: The USDT carve-out was checked explicitly and DOES NOT RESCUE this item: USDT does not revert on zero-value transfers, and the path is unreachable regardless, so the disposal does not depend on the class label at all.

findings.law3InventoryUpheld: SA-009 (Ownable-surface enumeration) is retained as INVENTORY only, and the deduplicator's critical caveat is endorsed and re-stated: nothing a competent owner would be SURPRISED by is suppressed under it. Every non-obvious footgun in those setters is filed separately - DEDUP-02-002 (registration liveness), DEDUP-02-005 (ownership transfer), DEDUP-02-008 (hook-token brick), and ledger M-03/M-04/F-01 (cap and pricing).
